title: Migrating legacy password hashes to scrypt
when: A user table already holds fast or unsalted hashes (md5, sha1, plain sha256) or old scrypt settings, and every account must move to strong scrypt without forcing all users to reset.
prompt:
Goal: Every stored password becomes a strong scrypt hash at once by wrapping the old hash, then turns into a direct hash at the next login.
Steps:
1. Tag rows by prefix: legacy "md5$<hex>", wrapped "scrypt-wrap$N$r$p$salt$key", direct "scrypt$N$r$p$salt$key".
2. scripts/wrap-hashes.mjs: for each legacy row store scrypt(oldHex, newSalt) as scrypt-wrap, in batches inside transactions, after a backup kept outside the repo.
3. Verify by prefix: scrypt-wrap first recomputes the old fast hash from the typed password, then scrypt over it; direct rows run scrypt on the password.
4. After a good login on a wrapped or weaker row, save a direct scrypt hash with current settings.
5. After a set period (say 90 days) expire leftover wrapped rows and send those users through reset.
6. Unknown users still cost one scrypt call against a dummy hash, so timing reveals nothing.
Quality bar:
- No row stays a bare fast hash after the script.
- The script can restart midway and logs counts only.
- Tests cover every prefix and the upgrade on login.
Pitfalls:
- Dropping the legacy column before sampling real logins.
- Fast replies for unknown users that reveal which accounts exist.
- An N so high that logins time out; aim near 100 ms.
Verify:
- [ ] Every row has a known prefix.
- [ ] Wrapped and direct rows both log in.
- [ ] Login upgrades wrapped rows.
- [ ] Unknown users cost one scrypt call.
Output: scripts/wrap-hashes.mjs, auth/password.mjs with the prefix switch, test/password-migration.test.mjs.

examples.input: nosso banco tem senhas em md5, como migrar sem resetar todo mundo
examples.output: wrap md5 in scrypt now, direct scrypt on next login, reset leftovers after 90 days
